title: Rescue beyond borders
news: The Indian Navy and IAF freed 20 Iranian fishermen from pirates, using calibrated non-kinetic measures; Iran called it a testament to friendship.
syllabus: Ethical issues in international relations; Compassion; Means and ends (use of force)
link: Saving foreign sailors shows that duty to human life does not stop at nationality, and choosing calibrated, minimum force shows that even security operations can be guided by proportionality. Ethics here also serves interest: compassion builds trust between nations.
question: "Humanitarian action can be the meeting point of ethics and national interest in international relations." Discuss with examples.

title: Dollar investors, rupee investors
news: Amid calls to cut taxes for foreign investors, the Finance Minister asked: 'If you pitch for dollar investors, what about rupee investors?'
syllabus: Impartiality and non-partisanship; Fairness in public policy
link: Public policy must treat like cases alike: concessions that favour foreign over domestic investors for the same income break fairness and impartiality, even when the aim of attracting capital is legitimate. Good ends do not justify unequal means.
question: "Fairness in public policy means treating like cases alike." Examine with an example from economic policy.

title: Andhra braces for landfall, rescue teams mobilised in Odisha as Murasu approaches
syllabus: GS3 › Disaster and disaster management · GS2 › Federalism: inter-state cooperation · GS1 › Cyclones · GS4 › Empathy and compassion
summary: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha prepared for Cyclone Murasu; Tamil Nadu sent 500 electricity staff to help Andhra restore power.
evolution: Cyclone Arnab's rains cause landslides in Odisha; 300 villages marooned in Ganjam (page 11).
Andhra braces for a second cyclone, Murasu (page 7).
Murasu nears landfall; Tamil Nadu sends power crews to Andhra.
ideas: Back-to-back cyclones: less than a week after Arnab, a severe cyclonic storm forced a second round of evacuations and school closures in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
GS1 · Cyclones / GS3 · Disaster management
Back-to-back cyclones test whether preparedness can be sustained, not just mounted once.
States help states: at Andhra's request, Tamil Nadu deployed 500 electricity department personnel in 25 teams to restore power.
GS2 · Cooperative federalism
Tamil Nadu's power crews for Andhra show cooperative federalism working horizontally, state to state.
Turning a hazard into a resource: Andhra's CM asked officials to use the heavy rainfall to fill tanks and reservoirs through efficient water management, and to finish restoration within 48 hours.
GS3 · Water management / DM
Linking flood response with reservoir filling turns a disaster into water security.
Impact beyond landfall: though landfall was in Andhra, Odisha's southern districts were put on high alert and evacuations prioritised.
GS3 · Disaster preparedness
Cyclone preparedness must cover neighbouring regions, not just the landfall zone.
keywords: Inter-state help in disasters is horizontal federalism in action.
States lending personnel and equipment in emergencies
Mutual-aid arrangements speed up restoration after disasters.
Time target to restore essential services
A 48-hour restoration target keeps recovery accountable.

Using cyclone rainfall to fill tanks and reservoirs
GS3 · Water management · GS3 · Disaster management
Andhra's plan to fill reservoirs from cyclone rain shows disasters can be managed for long-term gain.

answer.t: As Cyclone Murasu hit Andhra Pradesh days after Cyclone Arnab, Tamil Nadu sent 500 electricity staff in 25 teams to restore its neighbour's power.

answer.t: When a cyclone crosses a coastline, it erases state borders; India's federalism is strongest when its states respond as one.

title: Empathy across state lines
news: When Cyclone Murasu struck Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu sent 500 electricity workers in 25 teams to restore its neighbour's power.
syllabus: Empathy, compassion and tolerance towards the weaker sections; Public service values
link: Public service that ends at the state border is incomplete; helping a neighbouring state's people in a crisis shows empathy and solidarity as public values, beyond political rivalries.
question: "In a disaster, empathy must not stop at administrative boundaries." Discuss with examples.

title: 'I didn't sit on my sofa for a year': The cost of living with OCD
syllabus: GS2 › Issues relating to health (mental health) · GS4 › Empathy; Attitude and stigma
summary: Minor topic: personal accounts show how shame, misdiagnosis and late treatment turn obsessive-compulsive disorder into years of distress.
ideas: More than neatness: OCD is a mental health condition where intrusive thoughts trigger anxiety and repetitive rituals that bring only brief relief.
GS2 · Mental health
Popular misuse of 'OCD' trivialises a disabling mental illness.
The treatment gap: shame, misdiagnosis and confusion with religious practice delay care; most people live with symptoms for long before their first session.
GS2 · Health access
Stigma and low awareness widen India's mental-health treatment gap.
Treatable with the right care: medication with exposure and response prevention therapy is the standard; psychoeducation for families matters; advanced options such as deep TMS are free at AIIMS.
GS2 · Health services
Combining medication, therapy and family education makes OCD manageable.
keywords: Share of people with a condition who get no care
Delayed diagnosis widens the mental-health treatment gap.
Teaching patients and families about the condition
Psychoeducation reduces stigma and improves treatment success.
data: Prevalence of OCD among Indian adults
National Mental Health Survey (2015-16), via IE
The National Mental Health Survey estimated OCD prevalence among Indian adults at 0.8%.
examples: Young people hiding symptoms for years before diagnosis
GS2 · Mental health · GS4 · Empathy, attitude and stigma
OCD accounts show that empathy and awareness, not just medicines, decide whether people seek help.

title: A lifelong home: CSR with care
news: Reliance Foundation announced a 100-acre township near Mumbai as a lifelong home for orphaned children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, in family-style homes with caregivers.
syllabus: Ethics in business: corporate social responsibility; Compassion towards the weaker sections
link: CSR is most meaningful when it meets a lasting social need with dignity, here the anxiety of parents of children with disabilities about who will care for them; the test is sustained care, not announcement.
question: "Corporate social responsibility is an ethical commitment, not merely a legal obligation." Discuss with examples.
